solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Check carton isn’t damaged (10)

indicatorNotes.damaged: Something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

annotation.surface: A shopper inspects a parcel and finds the box is intact.
annotation.walkthrough: "Check" reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun: a check is a restraint.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a restraint that holds something back, as in keeping costs in check.

entries.clue: Finished on time, that’s obvious (5)

blocks.note: When something is finished it is over.
T is the standard abbreviation for time.

annotation.surface: Someone remarks that a job clearly came in on schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: "On" just places T after OVER in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, plain to see: obvious.

entries.clue: Little time for another helping (7)

blocks.note: A small unit of time, several of them.
A further plateful taken at a meal, in British and US usage alike.

annotation.surface: A diner has only a moment left but wants more food.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses of SECONDS: tiny units of time, and a further plateful at a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Asking for seconds is asking for another helping of food.

entries.clue: Fled wet weather, leaving island (3)

indicatorNotes.leaving: The island's letter leaves the word, so it is removed.

blocks.note: Wet weather is rain.
I is the standard abbreviation for island; take it out of RAIN.

annotation.surface: Holidaymakers escape the downpour by quitting an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove the I from RAIN to leave RAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Ran, as in ran away, is the past tense of flee.

entries.clue: Sienna set terribly unfeeling (9)

indicatorNotes.terribly: Done terribly, the letters come out badly arranged.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

annotation.surface: A woman called Sienna is described as coldly indifferent.
annotation.walkthrough: Sienna looks like a name (or a colour), but it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Insensate means lacking sensation or sympathy: unfeeling.

entries.clue: Singer given £10 note, I hear (5)

indicatorNotes.I hear: What I hear is a sound, so the answer sounds like the wordplay.

blocks.note: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.

annotation.surface: A performer is paid with a ten-pound note.
annotation.walkthrough: A tenner is everyday British slang for a £10 note; spoken, it matches TENOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

entries.clue: High as a kite, as Olive might be (6)

blocks.note: Slang for heavily intoxicated on cannabis or other drugs.
An olive may have its pit taken out before serving.

annotation.surface: Someone called Olive is suspected of being very high.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital makes Olive look like a woman's name; it is the fruit, whose pit is called a stone.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang sense: intoxicated on drugs; the other sense is an olive with its pit removed.

entries.clue: Act as a prisoner’s guiding light (6)

blocks.note: To act as something is to be it.
Used as written.
A con is a convict, a prisoner.

annotation.surface: Someone serves as the light that guides a prisoner.
annotation.walkthrough: "Act as" looks like one phrase, but "as" is only surface glue and "Act" alone gives BE.
annotation.definitionFit: A beacon is a light or fire used as a signal or guide.

entries.clue: Boy at back tackling advanced piece of music (6)

indicatorNotes.at back: AT goes at the back of the boy.
indicatorNotes.tackling: Tackling means taking on, so A is added next.

blocks.note: A boy is a son.
Used as written.
A is the standard abbreviation for advanced.

annotation.surface: A young footballer at the back makes a tackle and pushes forward.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture hides simple assembly: SON with AT behind it, then A.
annotation.definitionFit: A sonata is a composition for one or two instruments.

entries.clue: Shock fans from the east (4)

indicatorNotes.from the east: Read from the east, i.e. right to left in an across clue.

blocks.note: Fans of something are nuts, enthusiasts.

annotation.surface: Supporters from the east are left shocked.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fans" means enthusiasts, as in football nuts, not cooling devices.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to daze or astonish someone.

entries.clue: Challenge Charlie about appearance (8)

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet.
About, as in a talk on a subject, is ON.
A front is an outward show or appearance.

annotation.surface: Someone takes Charlie to task over how he looks.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" is not a container here; it simply gives ON, as in a book on birds.
annotation.definitionFit: To confront someone is to challenge them face to face.

entries.clue: Lizard messing up clean home (9)

indicatorNotes.messing up: Messing up puts the letters into disorder.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

annotation.surface: A pet lizard makes a mess of a tidy house.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads naturally as a lizard wrecking a house; the whole of "clean home" is the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a lizard famous for changing colour to match its surroundings.

entries.clue: Not all change is hard for hostess (6)

indicatorNotes.Not all: Only part of the following words is used.

blocks.note: chanGE IS HArd.

annotation.surface: Adapting is difficult for the woman running a party.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word breaks in "change is hard".
annotation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain and host guests.

entries.clue: Team still holding the French (6)

indicatorNotes.holding: One word holds the other inside it.

blocks.note: Still, as in still better, can mean even.
LE is French for the.

annotation.surface: A squad keeps hold of some French players.
annotation.walkthrough: "Still" in the sense of "still more" means even, not motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has eleven players, so is called an eleven.

entries.clue: Quarrelling when around Fleet Street barber? (2,4)

indicatorNotes.around: One word goes around the other.

blocks.note: When and as are interchangeable, as in as I arrived.
Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street.

annotation.surface: People fall out over a barber on Fleet Street.
annotation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is a London street, home of the fictional murderous barber Sweeney Todd of the musical.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: people in disagreement are said to be at odds with each other.

entries.clue: Old boy’s remedy is little known (7)

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil; add the S.
A remedy is a cure.

annotation.surface: A former pupil's treatment turns out to be little known.
annotation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school, abbreviated OB; the possessive S is kept.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: not widely known about, like an obscure poet.

entries.clue: Seek Nero out for something to fan the flames? (8)

indicatorNotes.out: Out, as in out of order, signals the letters are rearranged.

blocks.note: The letters to rearrange.

annotation.surface: Hunting the emperor Nero, who fiddled while Rome burned, for fuel to spread the fire.
annotation.walkthrough: Nero is linked to the burning of Rome, so the fire picture fits; the question mark flags that the definition is loose.
annotation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin, a fuel that feeds a fire.

entries.clue: Booze supplier contributing to giftshop tickets (5)

indicatorNotes.contributing to: The answer contributes letters to the words that follow.

blocks.note: giftshOP TICkets.

annotation.surface: A drinks firm sponsors tickets sold at a gift shop.
annotation.walkthrough: An optic is a British pub device fixed to an upside-down spirits bottle that dispenses a measured shot.
annotation.definitionFit: An optic supplies spirits in exact measures behind a bar.

entries.clue: Betray group of agents to dictator (4)

indicatorNotes.to dictator: A dictator here is someone dictating, speaking words out loud, so we go by sound.

blocks.note: A cell is a small group of spies or agents.

annotation.surface: A spy ring is handed over to a tyrant.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dictator" suggests a tyrant, but here it is someone who dictates, speaking words for another to write down.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to sell someone down the river is to betray them.

entries.clue: Call up about one’s flowering plant (5)

indicatorNotes.up: In a down clue, up means read from bottom to top.
indicatorNotes.about: The word goes about, around, the other.

blocks.note: Used as written.
One is I, the Roman numeral.

annotation.surface: Someone phones to talk about their lilac bush.
annotation.walkthrough: Put I inside CALL to make CALIL, then read it upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white flowers.

entries.clue: Decide on pay (6)

blocks.note: To reach a decision about something, like a date.
To pay what is owed, as with a bill or account.

annotation.surface: Two parties agree what the wage will be.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as "decide on the pay"; split it after "on".
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to fix on a choice, and to clear a bill.

entries.clue: Sally regularly holds cup in self-satisfied way (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Take letters at regular intervals: S, L, Y.
indicatorNotes.holds: The outer word holds the other inside it.

blocks.note: The first, third and fifth letters of Sally.
A mug is a cup.

annotation.surface: A woman called Sally clutches her cup looking pleased with herself.
annotation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name but is only a source of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in a complacent, pleased-with-oneself manner.

entries.clue: So fed up, having lost £1000 (3)

indicatorNotes.having lost: The word has lost a letter, which is removed.

blocks.note: Fed up, as in sick of it.
K stands for a thousand, as in £5k; remove it.

annotation.surface: Someone is so fed up after losing a thousand pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: "So" looks like an intensifier for "fed up"; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: the Latin word for thus, printed in quotations to mark an error as original.

entries.clue: Voice telling you what’s wrong with Conservative discipline (10)

blocks.note: CON is the standard abbreviation for Conservative.
A discipline is a field of study, such as a science.

annotation.surface: Someone's inner voice objects to Tory-style strictness.
annotation.walkthrough: Conservative refers to the British Tory party; "discipline" means a subject of study, not punishment.
annotation.definitionFit: Your conscience is the inner voice that tells you right from wrong.
